cards.title: Why Do Controlling Parents Praise More?
cards.body: Excessive praise from controlling parents can inflate children's egos and create unhealthy self-perception. Understanding the psychology behind this behavior helps parents adjust their approach to support genuine confidence.

cards.title: The "I'm Bored" Trap Isn't About Your Kid's Brain
cards.body: Children's boredom often reflects parents' discomfort with silence rather than a problem kids need to solve. Learning to sit with quiet moments teaches kids valuable self-regulation skills.

cards.title: We Turned "Let Them" Into a Mantra But Skipped the Hard Part
cards.body: The "let them" parenting philosophy requires emotional education to work effectively. Without teaching kids how to manage feelings, the concept falls short of its potential.

cards.title: Summer + Co-parenting = Can Cause Anxiety
cards.body: Summer schedules and custody transitions create unique stress for co-parenting families. Strategic planning and communication help reduce anxiety during extended time-sharing arrangements.

cards.title: Teaching the Next Generation to Reject Misogyny
cards.body: Misogyny is learned through family, culture, and media—but parents can teach children to reject it. Raising kids who embrace equality and support other women starts with modeling these values.

cards.title: Why Your Adult Child's Diagnosis May Be the Problem
cards.body: Labels that helped during childhood can sometimes hold adult children back from growth. Parents may need to shift their perspective when diagnoses become limitations rather than explanations.

cards.title: When Regret Finds Its Voice
cards.body: Fathers who move beyond silent reflection and courageously revisit painful moments with their children create opportunities for healing. Open dialogue replaces silence with understanding and connection.

cards.title: An Act of Kindness Teaches Kids About Community
cards.body: Teaching children about mitzvah and kindness helps them develop empathy and notice others' needs. Parents who model caring behavior raise kids invested in making the world better.

cards.title: I Was a Terrible Teen, Now My Son Is One
cards.body: Parenting a difficult adolescent becomes easier when you recognize your own teen years with humor and humility. Understanding your own patterns helps you respond with patience rather than judgment.

cards.title: Why Ask New Mothers What They Actually Think?
cards.body: Declining birthrates reflect deep anxieties among mothers that policy makers often overlook. Listening to mothers' real concerns—not offering medals or cash—is key to supporting families.

cards.title: Why Attachment Theory Is Everywhere Right Now
cards.body: Attachment theory explains how early relationships shape children's emotional development and future connections. Understanding your own attachment style helps you parent more effectively and build healthier bonds.
